title: perf(canary): adaptive thresholds and hysteresis for automated regression detection and rollout guards
author: Avery Chen
description: Context: Our performance canaries detect latency/throughput regressions and gate rollouts, but we've seen noise (transient spikes, KV-cache TTL effects) causing false positives and unnecessary rollbacks. This PR implements adaptive thresholds and hysteresis that make detection resilient to workload variance and KV cache warmup patterns. Summary of changes: 1) Add adaptive thresholding algorithm that adjusts sensitivity based on short-term baseline statistics (p50/p95/p99 smoothing) and historical noise levels. 2) Introduce hysteresis state machine to require sustained breach over configurable windows and to avoid flip-flopping during transient spikes. 3) KV-cache-aware modifiers so low hit-rate periods temporarily relax thresholds while cache warms. 4) Add metric labels and trace spans for canary decision path to improve observability and postmortem analysis. 5) New unit and integration tests for edge cases and replayed incident traces. Why: Reduce false-positive canary aborts, reduce unnecessary rollbacks, and increase overall rollout throughput while maintaining safety. Backwards compatibility: defaults preserve current thresholds; config flags allow opt-in of aggressive mode. Rollout plan: staged rollout to internal canaries -> 20% of customer rollouts for 48h -> full. Monitoring: dashboards added and alerts tuned (see release_notes). Misc: Linear tasks ENG-2142 and ENG-2301 track follow-ups (threshold tuning UI, canary config API).
